statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, while the weekend futures halt limits evidence quality rather than signalling stress.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains EA_ON with Tail at 5%. A narrow elevated-uncertainty window is published around the Sunday 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, where a weekend gap would meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. Stress is moderate on a hiking Fed, a near-5% 10-year yield and contested Strait of Hormuz oil flows.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail low after an orderly Friday close; narrow reopen window flagged
body: Assessment is made during the CME weekend halt, so no live NQ price path is observable. The standing reference is Friday's close at 29,644.17 (+0.67%), struck in the upper part of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range, with VIX easing to 14.81 (-4.08%). Cross-asset context is coherent rather than conflicting: the 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 5% and the 2-year near 4.67% after the FOMC raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 17 September, its first hike in three years, while WTI eased to about $100.30 in a third consecutive decline. Friday's tape showed strong semiconductor leadership against a split megacap complex, which argues for two-way trade rather than persistent directional structure. Tail stays low because none of the conditions that define a pathological no-retracement path can be observed while the venue is shut, and Friday's session ended in orderly fashion. Stress is moderate, reflecting a hawkish Fed with October hike odds priced above 50%, elevated oil, and an active US-Iran tanker conflict in the Strait of Hormuz that leaves genuine weekend headline risk. Confidence is solid but tempered: current levels, yields, oil, volatility and the forward calendar are all verified, yet no continuous price path exists to confirm them. The single narrow danger window covers the Sunday reopen, where any weekend repricing would be expressed as a gap into thin liquidity.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe a stable, low-Tail regime. Tail held between 4% and 5% throughout, mapping to EA_ON and green in every hour, while Stress drifted up from 24% late on 19 September to 33% by the 16:00-17:00 UTC hours as the hawkish Fed repricing and elevated oil backdrop accumulated. Confidence ranged from 71% to 76%, easing late in the window as the weekend halt removed live price-path evidence. Dominant mode was recorded as normal in all 24 hours, with no interval showing the persistent one-way structure that would justify a higher Tail reading.
outlookSummary: The cycle spans the remainder of the CME weekend halt, the Sunday 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the Asian and European sessions, and the Monday US cash session through 18:00 UTC. Tail is projected to stay in the low band throughout, peaking at 11% around the US cash open and at 9% at the reopen, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON in all 24 hours. The two structurally meaningful checkpoints are the reopen, where any weekend Hormuz or summit-related repricing would arrive as a gap into thin liquidity, and the 13:30 UTC opening auction, which is the cycle's most reliable generator of genuine directional structure. Monday carries only second-tier US data and Fed commentary at 10:30 UTC; the week's larger catalysts, flash PMIs on 23 September and the scheduled US-China summit on 24-25 September, fall beyond this window and are carried in the event calendar. Projections are conditional: apart from the current clock hour, no future price-path structure is treated as already observed.
